guided.files.none: This import has no files yet.
guided.files.choose: Choose a folder on the start page
guided.files.error: We could not read this folder: {message}
guided.files.againJob: We are looking again. This takes a while for a large folder. You can leave this page.
guided.found.lede: We looked at your {files} files. They make
guided.found.gloss: An item is one thing in Omeka, such as a letter or a photo, with its files and its details.
guided.found.ask: Does one item have more than one file, such as a front and a back, or pages?
guided.found.now: Right now, files are one item only when their names are the same except for the ending, such as “Scan 3.pdf” and “Scan 3.jpg”. We do not guess more than that. Show us one example and we read every name the same way.
guided.found.marked: Files are one item when their names differ only in the part you marked: {marks}.
guided.found.typed: You changed how names are read in Advanced mode.
guided.found.ungrouped: The files are not put into items yet, so they make no items. This was chosen in Advanced mode.
guided.found.later: You can change any answer later.
guided.found.notMedia: We left out {count} files that are not a picture, a sound, a film or a PDF. We read the first bytes of each file to know.
guided.found.notMediaOne: We left out 1 file that is not a picture, a sound, a film or a PDF. We read the first bytes of each file to know.
guided.example.choose: Choose one file of an item that has more than one file.
guided.example.findHint: Part of a file name, such as front
guided.example.noName: No file name with more than one part has this text.
guided.example.parts: Here is the name of the file you chose, in its parts.
guided.example.click: Click the part that changes between the files of this item.
guided.example.clickHint: For example, “front” and “back”, or “page 001” and “page 002”. One click marks that part and every part after it, up to the ending. The first part starts the name of the item, so it cannot be the part that changes.
guided.example.whatHere: What is in this place in your other names?
guided.example.onlyTicked: Only the words I tick below
guided.example.wordsLede: These words are in the same place in names with as many parts as this one, with how many files have each. Tick the ones that mean another file of one item.
guided.example.others: and {count} others. Search to find one.
guided.example.make: With this, your files make {count} items:
guided.example.makeOne: With this, your files make 1 item:
guided.list.none: We found no list in your folder.
guided.list.whatShort: A list has one row for each item.
guided.list.pairBy: Pair each row with an item by the column
guided.list.otherFiles: {count} rows name another file of an item
guided.list.otherFilesOne: 1 row names another file of an item
guided.list.oneEach: No two rows name files of one item
guided.list.readAs: Its bytes read as {kind} text. Change it in Advanced.
guided.list.helpPaired: Rows paired: the rows that name one of your files or items. “Ignoring case, zeros and _ - .” also pairs a name that differs only in capital letters, in zeros at the start, or in those signs.
guided.list.codeGloss: An item’s code is the part of its file names that is the same for all its files.
guided.list.helpRowIs: A row is: what one row of the list describes. ✓ marks the answer that the rows suggest.
guided.list.columnsLede: A column goes into the field with the same name. Choose a field for the others. Your answer counts for every row.
guided.list.levelLede: On the item: the values of all its rows, each value once. On each file: the values of that file’s own row. We suggest each file where the values differ inside some item, and the item where they never do.
guided.list.moreFields: Here you see the Dublin Core fields. Every other field is in Advanced mode.
guided.where.setsAsk: Which item set should each item go into?
guided.where.setsGloss: An item set is a collection of items in Omeka.
guided.where.setLeaf: One item set for each folder
guided.where.setTop: One item set for each top folder
guided.where.setOne: One new item set for everything, named “{name}”
guided.where.setOld: An item set already in Omeka
guided.where.setsNone: Items are in no item set.
guided.where.typesAsk: What kind of item is each one?
guided.where.typesGloss: An item type is the kind of item. It decides which fields the item has.
guided.where.fromTop: The top folder of each file
guided.where.typesEmpty: No item has a value here yet.
guided.where.valuesNote: Choose an item type for each. Values that are written differently, such as “Letter” and “Letters”, are different values: choose the same item type for both.
guided.where.spellings: {count} spellings that differ only in capital letters or spaces. We treat them as one.
guided.check.once: We ask once for each kind of problem, not once for each item. Each has a suggested answer. If you skip one, we use its suggested answer.
guided.check.nothing: Nothing to answer. Your files and your list are ready to add.
guided.check.mustFix: This must be fixed before you can add.
guided.check.fileRowsWhy: Some rows of your list name another file of an item that a row already names. Such a list may have one row for each file.
guided.check.cells: {count} rows of your list have the wrong number of cells.
guided.check.cellsOne: 1 row of your list has the wrong number of cells.
guided.check.cellsWhy: A quotation mark is not closed, or the row has too few or too many cells.
guided.check.cellsLeave: Add the files without the row
guided.check.cellsKeep: Use the cells we could read
guided.check.noFile: {count} rows of your list name no file of this import.
guided.check.noFileOne: 1 row of your list names no file of this import.
guided.check.noFileWhy: No file has the name or the code that the row gives.
guided.check.noFileKeep: Add them as items with no file
guided.check.noRow: {count} items have files but no row in your list.
guided.check.noRowOne: 1 item has files but no row in your list.
guided.check.noRowWhy: No row gives their name or their code.
guided.check.same: {count} files are byte for byte the same as another file.
guided.check.sameOne: 1 file is byte for byte the same as another file.
guided.check.sameWhy: They have the same size and the same contents.
guided.check.sameOneKept: Leave out one file of each pair: the one your list does not name
guided.check.noFit: {count} files have a name that does not fit the example you marked.
guided.check.noFitOne: 1 file has a name that does not fit the example you marked.
guided.check.noFitPlain: {count} files have a name that does not fit how the other files are grouped into items.
guided.check.noFitPlainOne: 1 file has a name that does not fit how the other files are grouped into items.
guided.check.noFitOwn: Make each one an item of its own
guided.check.knownWhy: Omeka has an item with the same identifier.
guided.check.knownLeave: Skip them. Keep the ones in Omeka
guided.check.knownKeep: Add them again, as second items
guided.check.date: {count} dates are not in a form Omeka can sort.
guided.check.dateOne: 1 date is not in a form Omeka can sort.
guided.check.dateWhy: Omeka sorts dates written as 1950, 1950-08 or 1950-08-15. It keeps other text as written, but a search by date does not find it.
guided.check.untitled: {count} items to add have no title.
guided.check.untitledOne: 1 item to add has no title.
guided.check.noTitleKeep: Add them without a title. The admin lists them as untitled
guided.check.noTitleCode: Use the item code as the title
guided.check.noTitleName: Use the file name as the title
guided.check.type: {count} items have an item type that Omeka does not have.
guided.check.typeOne: 1 item has an item type that Omeka does not have.
guided.check.typeWhy: You can choose an item type for each of these values on “Where they go”.
guided.check.typeKeep: Add them with no item type
guided.check.refused: {count} files in your list are of a type this Omeka does not accept.
guided.check.refusedOne: 1 file in your list is of a type this Omeka does not accept.
guided.check.refusedWhy: The file settings of this Omeka refuse these types, so we leave them out.
guided.check.refusedSettings: Change the allowed file types in Settings
guided.check.handled: We took care of {count} small things
guided.check.handledOne: We took care of 1 small thing
guided.check.handledSpaces: {count} values had spaces at the start or end. We took them off.
guided.check.handledNotMedia: {count} files are not a picture, a sound, a film or a PDF. We left them out.
guided.add.append: add the list’s details to items already in Omeka
guided.add.revise: change the details the list gives, and keep the rest
guided.add.update: change the details the list gives; an empty cell clears that detail
guided.add.replace: remove all details of items already in Omeka, then write the list’s
guided.add.delete: delete from Omeka the items the list names
guided.add.inPlace: To change items already in Omeka in place of adding new ones, use Advanced mode.
guided.add.chosenAdvanced: You chose this in Advanced mode.
guided.add.mustFix: {count} problems must be fixed before you can add.
guided.add.mustFixOne: 1 problem must be fixed before you can add.
guided.add.undo: You can undo the whole import later.
guided.add.titleCode: Items with no title get their item code as the title.
guided.add.fileRows: Each row of “{name}” describes one file.
